chief_complaint: bulbous, enlarged, and nodular nose with prominent pores secondary to end-stage rosacea
hpi_details: 65M with chronic severe rosacea presenting with grotesque, cauliflower-like hypertrophy of sebaceous glands and skin of nasal tip and alae undergoing loop electrocautery / CO2 laser surgical contouring and debulking.
ideas: He thinks his chronic facial flushing and clogged pores caused the oil glands in his nose to overproduce and turn into lumpy excess skin.
concerns: He is deeply humiliated because strangers assume his enlarged red nose means he is an alcoholic, causing him to withdraw from social life and avoid seeing friends.
expectations: He hopes the surgeon can use a laser or surgical shaving to remove the thick excess tissue so his nose returns to a natural shape.

history.answer: My nose has become terribly swollen, bumpy, and red over the past few years, and it's getting so bulbous and heavy that I can barely recognize myself.
The swelling and bumpy texture on my nose first started about five years ago, although my cheeks and nose have been prone to redness for well over ten years.
It grew very slowly at first, but over the last couple of years the cauliflower-like lumps have thickened much more rapidly.
It is concentrated right on the tip and sides of my nose, with some redness spreading across my cheeks.
It is one large, confluent, lobular mass covering the lower half of my nose, and I do not have lumps like this anywhere else on my body.
The tissue feels firm and rubbery, not soft or fluctuant, and it doesn't slip or slide around beneath the skin.
No, it doesn't ache or hurt at all, even when I touch or press on it.
The skin looks purplish-red with prominent spider veins, but I haven't noticed any dark brown or black spots developing.
No spontaneous bleeding, and there are no open sores or persistent scabs that refuse to heal.
My nose stays flushed and reddish, but it doesn't feel warm to the touch and there is no foul-smelling drainage or pus leaking out.
If I squeeze the enlarged pores, a little bit of thick white-yellow sebum comes out, but there is no central opening like a cyst.
The swelling never shrinks or goes away; it stays continuously enlarged, though the redness flushes brighter when I am in the heat.
I have never injured my nose or had surgery on my face, but a dermatologist told me years ago that I have chronic rosacea.
Years ago I used metronidazole cream and took doxycycline pills for my rosacea, but they stopped helping once this thick fibrous tissue built up.
The sheer weight of the thickened skin pulls down on my nostrils, which partially blocks my airflow and makes it harder to breathe through my nose at night.
I have spent a moderate amount of time outdoors gardening over the years, but I have never suffered severe or blistering sunburns.
No, neither I nor anyone in my family has ever been diagnosed with melanoma or any type of skin cancer.

history.answer: I have not had any fevers, chills, unexplained weight loss, or swollen glands in my neck.
No, I don't have diabetes, I've never received an organ transplant, and I take no immunosuppressive medications.
It is deeply embarrassing to go out because strangers stare at me and assume I am a heavy drinker, so I've been avoiding social events and staying home.
I figured my chronic facial redness and clogged pores just got out of hand and caused the oil glands in my nose to swell into thick, bumpy tissue over time.
I feel so humiliated because everyone assumes I'm a heavy drinker when they see my nose, and it's gotten so bad that I avoid going out in public or seeing friends altogether.
I'm hoping you can shave down or laser away all this lumpy excess skin so my nose looks like a normal shape again.
I do not have any chronic medical conditions like high blood pressure, diabetes, or heart disease.
I had an appendectomy when I was a teenager, but I have never had any other surgeries or hospitalizations.
I do not take any regular prescription medications, over-the-counter drugs, or herbal supplements.
I have no known allergies to medications, foods, or materials like latex.
I have never smoked cigarettes or used tobacco products.
I only drink an occasional glass of wine once or twice a month, despite people unfairly assuming my red nose is from alcohol abuse.
I am a retired high school teacher living with my wife, and I stay active by taking walks and tending to my garden.
My father had hypertension, but there is no family history of rosacea, rhinophyma, or skin malignancies.

exam.finding: Blood pressure 124/78 mmHg, heart rate 68 beats/min, respiratory rate 14 breaths/min, oxygen saturation 98% on room air, body temperature 36.7°C.
Comfortable-appearing older man in no acute distress, with prominent bulbous facial and nasal enlargement.

Marked bulbous, lobular, cauliflower-like soft tissue hypertrophy involving the nasal tip and bilateral alae, with patulous dilated pores, prominent telangiectasias, and non-tender rubbery firmness; no ulceration, crusting, or suspicious discrete pigmented lesions.

External compression and narrowing of both nasal valves due to overgrown redundant skin and sebaceous tissue; anterior rhinoscopy shows patent mucosal airway without polyps, masses, or septal perforation; posterior oropharynx is normal.
No preauricular, submandibular, submental, or cervical lymphadenopathy palpable bilaterally.
Mild conjunctival injection and mild bilateral eyelid margin telangiectasia consistent with ocular rosacea; pupils equal, round, and reactive to light with full extraocular movements.
Regular rate and rhythm with normal first and second heart sounds; no murmurs, rubs, or gallops heard.
Lungs clear to auscultation bilaterally with vesicular breath sounds; no wheezing, rhonchi, or crackles.
